x: Later, at the "Black Swan", the Poly and Surrey A.C. found to their surprise that Gerry and the Pacemakers were still in very good voice The high spirits prevailed to the Social on the 26th October when we had well over 100 people in attendance.

Well, with Geoff North and John Thresher running into form at the right time Gerry should get peak support. At the time of writing Fairclough and Major seem to be humming along and Mann is just the runner to give them all a great start.

Last year, Gerry was 17th, and is perfectly capable of leading the team again with a place in the first 20. Now over the past four years, here are the best positions of some of our other runners, and these are not necessarily the best of which they are capable:
Leading for the first mile, Gerry was then caught by Gary McIlroy of Epsom and Belgrave's Jim Estall, and the three fought tooth and nail, swapping the lead over the next three miles.
No problems on the last lap as Gerry carried the Bels away from any danger of finishing out of the frame, gaining half a minute on AFD and a whole minute on Boxhill.
The melee of the second leg saw wholesale changes in the team positions and Said slipped back six places although he was pleased with his time in relation to Cap'n Gerry's.

Now Gerry likes a fast start while Ray Foley prefers to come through as the race progresses, so it was a surprise when the runners poured out of the woods at the end of lap one and it was Ray heading our Captain as they slithered across the muddy playing fields in the bunch chasing Ranelagh's Dave Benton.

It was 6, 7, 10, 12, 19, and when 'Gerry' and Phil Carstairs came in (good run from Phil) we went into the lead. We knew it was going to be close – and nowhere near the clawback of points that we needed – and as it happened Herne Hill, with their men still all in 48, took another 26 points out of us…

One of the Club's keenest supporters, Mavis was the daughter of Belgrave's respected runner and Past President, Tom Morrell. Being a member of the Morrell family also meant that Mavis had a very formidable list of honorary uncles to help keep an eye on her - Uncle "Gerry", known more familiarly to u…
No sooner had our story about Belgrave’s best 5 miles times been posted on the website when Gerry North was on the phone, reminding us about the Bracknell ‘5’ of August 3, 1968.
